title: Avo-6-Part-2
description: Comprehensive avionics Part 2 exam covering satellite communication, HF/VHF communication, SELCAL, microphones, interphone systems, ELT, CVR, PA systems, bonding, and aircraft communication systems.

questions.question: Which satellite is synchronous with Earth's orbit?
questions.explanation: The module describes GEO (geostationary) satellites as satellites synchronized with Earth's rotation, so they appear fixed relative to the ground.

questions.question: Which is a programmable switch module?
questions.explanation: SELCAL uses a programmable code to selectively call an aircraft, reducing the need for continuous voice monitoring.

questions.question: For MIC, which is a radio communication system?
questions.explanation: The flight interphone is part of the aircraft communication/audio system used by flight crew to access and use radio communications.

questions.question: Which of the following devices acts differently in working principle?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is retained from the question bank. The communication module describes different microphone types by their transduction principles, including carbon, moving-coil, crystal and electrostatic types.

questions.question: In the microphone, which parameter moves the diaphragm?
questions.explanation: A microphone diaphragm is moved by the acoustic pressure variations of the sound wave.

questions.question: Which system provides the flight crew and cabin crew with a means of making announcements and distributing music to passengers through cabin speakers?
questions.explanation: The passenger address (PA) system distributes crew announcements and music to passengers through cabin speakers.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a service interphone?
questions.explanation: Antenna is not a service-interphone component; service interphone equipment includes jacks and associated communication circuitry.

questions.question: In the call system, the call light on the passenger signs panel comes on and the warning module gives HI chime. Which call is indicated?
questions.explanation: The stated indication corresponds to an attendant-to-flight-compartment call in the cabin call system.

questions.question: What is the location of service interphone jacks?
questions.explanation: The question bank identifies the APU compartment as a location for service interphone jacks; exact installation locations are aircraft-type dependent.

questions.question: Which units provide microphone selector push buttons and listen switches for VHF communication systems?
questions.explanation: Audio control/selector panels provide microphone selection and listening controls for aircraft communication systems.

questions.question: SELCAL ID for the aircraft is set in the:
questions.explanation: The SELCAL aircraft code is set/programmed through the applicable program switch.

questions.question: The frequency range of VHF is:
questions.explanation: The module's VHF communication section uses the aircraft VHF communication band around 118–137 MHz.

questions.question: An automatically activated ELT that is permanently attached to an aircraft is called:
questions.explanation: An Automatic Fixed ELT is permanently installed on the aircraft and activates automatically under its specified activation conditions.

questions.question: What is the color of the CVR box?
questions.explanation: CVR units are commonly housed in highly visible orange crash-protected enclosures.

questions.question: The basic purpose of a distress radio beacon is to help rescuers find survivors within the golden day. The golden day represents:
options: C. The first 24 hours following traumatic event
questions.explanation: The question bank defines the golden day as the first 24 hours following a traumatic event, when rapid location and rescue are particularly important.

questions.question: Which is not a use of static dischargers?
options: A. It radiates radio frequencies that interfere with radio and navigation equipment
questions.explanation: Static dischargers are intended to dissipate accumulated static electricity and reduce radio interference; they are not intended to radiate interfering RF.

questions.question: Static discharge is not located on the:
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is retained. Static-discharge devices are normally installed at aircraft extremities such as wing and tail surfaces; installation details depend on aircraft type.

questions.question: A passive satellite:
options: B. Generates a new carrier signal
C. transfer the signal without any amplification
questions.explanation: A passive satellite retransmits a received signal without active amplification.

questions.question: What is the common frequency range of HF communication?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer gives the HF range as 2–29.9 MHz; the module's HF section covers long-range HF communication using ionospheric propagation.

questions.question: SELCAL uses:
questions.explanation: SELCAL can operate with the aircraft's HF and VHF communication systems to provide selective alerting.

questions.question: HF communication using ionospheric and earth-surface reflections over long distances is also called:
questions.explanation: HF signals reflected by the ionosphere and earth surface can travel beyond line-of-sight distances; this is called sky-wave propagation.

questions.question: Which ELT is rigidly attached to an aircraft and automatically deployed and activated by impact and, in some cases, by hydrostatic sensors?
questions.explanation: An Automatic Deployable ELT is designed to deploy and activate automatically under specified impact or sensor conditions.

questions.question: A microphone (MIC) is a:
questions.explanation: A microphone is an electroacoustic transducer that converts acoustic energy into an electrical signal.

questions.question: Which principle varies the capacitor value?
questions.explanation: In an electrostatic microphone, diaphragm movement changes the distance between capacitor plates, changing capacitance.

questions.question: What is the function of PTT?
options: A. to change transceiver from the reception mode to transmission mode
B. To select the audio volume
C. To change the transceiver to receive mode
questions.explanation: PTT changes the communication system from reception to transmission when activated.

questions.question: Which gain antenna is used for medium quality voice / fax / data?
questions.explanation: The source identifies Aero H as the antenna used for the stated medium-quality voice/fax/data application.

questions.question: What is the purpose of muting local speaker transmission or interphone system?
options: C. To prevent acoustic feedback whistling noise
questions.explanation: Speaker muting during radio transmission or interphone operation prevents acoustic feedback, which can produce whistling.

questions.question: Cabin call and flight deck are unable but PA and ground call work. Which system should be checked?
questions.explanation: If PA and ground call operate while cabin call/flight-deck functions fail, the cabin interface is a logical area to check according to the question bank.

questions.question: Which device is used to measure the sound pressure levels?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is retained from the question bank. The module explains that microphones are acoustic transducers and discusses microphone output and sound-pressure conversion.

questions.question: Minor arcing between a hinge of flight control surface and the wing: what is the most probable corrective action?
options: C. missing or bad bonding, Install repair bonding strap
questions.explanation: Arcing across aircraft structural joints can indicate inadequate bonding. Repairing or installing the appropriate bonding strap restores the intended low-resistance electrical path.

questions.question: During pre-flight checks, the flight crew hears a horn sounding in the nose wheel well area. No chimes are heard in the cockpit and no cockpit switches were activated. What is the most probable cause?
options: A. The external service interphone call button was pressed by ground crew
questions.explanation: A horn in the nose-wheel area can be caused by the external service-interphone call button being operated by ground personnel.

questions.question: The ELT battery is replaceable every ___ years.
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is 2 years; battery replacement intervals are subject to the applicable ELT maintenance instructions and installation.

questions.question: What is the Cospas-Sarsat satellite frequency?
questions.explanation: Cospas-Sarsat distress beacon systems use 406 MHz for the encoded distress signal.

questions.question: Which panel is used to select the frequency of any VHF common radio?
questions.explanation: The radio communication panel is used to select and control the operating frequency of the applicable VHF communication radio.

questions.question: Which is not a function/advantage of HF?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is retained from the source. HF provides long-range communication, while the exact quality and reliability of voice transmission depend on propagation conditions.

questions.question: Flight crew initialize communication using ___ and ground station uses ___.
options: A. Polled mode and demand zone
B. SELCAL mode and scan mode
C. Demand zone and polled mode
questions.explanation: The question bank identifies demand-zone/polled-mode operation for the stated aircraft/ground communication initialization arrangement.

questions.question: VHF Communication is:
questions.explanation: VHF aircraft communication normally uses space-wave propagation and is therefore principally line-of-sight.

questions.question: Which one does not pass through REU?
questions.explanation: The source distinguishes the remote/area microphone from the individual cockpit microphone inputs routed through the REU.

questions.question: Which is not true about SELCAL?
options: B. Uses a four-letter aircraft code
questions.explanation: SELCAL is intended to provide selective alerting rather than continuous voice monitoring of the communication channels.

questions.question: When can the CVR be erased?
options: A. The A/C is on Ground and parking brake is set
B. During flight with parking brake released
C. Whenever the CVR circuit breaker is pulled
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is retained from the source; CVR erase operation is controlled by aircraft-specific logic and ground conditions to prevent accidental erasure in flight.

questions.question: Which is not a purpose of HF Control panel?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is retained. HF control panels are used for functions such as frequency/control selection; the exact control set is aircraft dependent.

questions.question: The universally recognized emergency frequency used for VHF communication is:
questions.explanation: 121.5 MHz is the internationally recognized VHF aeronautical emergency frequency.

questions.question: Which letters are not used?
questions.explanation: I, N and O are excluded from the relevant letter set to avoid ambiguity in the SELCAL coding scheme.

questions.question: Aircraft satellite communication uses ___ band during transmitting between aircraft and ___ band for ground station.
questions.explanation: The source identifies L-band for the aircraft-to-satellite link and C-band for the ground-side link in the stated SATCOM arrangement.

questions.question: Which is not true about HF radio communication?
options: C. It only uses line of sight propagation
questions.explanation: HF communication can use ionospheric/sky-wave propagation, so it is not limited to line-of-sight propagation.

questions.question: The flight interphone system is used for:
options: A. Cabin crews to communicate with each other and to ground crew
B. Flight crew and ground crew only
questions.explanation: The flight interphone provides communication among crew and interfaces with other aircraft communication systems; the supplied answer is retained from the source.

questions.question: Which device is used to delete recorded data?
questions.explanation: An erase switch is used to initiate deletion of recorded CVR data under the permitted ground conditions.

questions.question: A microphone that controls resistance by varying current is a:
questions.explanation: A carbon microphone varies the resistance of carbon granules as diaphragm movement changes their compression, producing a corresponding electrical variation.

questions.question: What is the use of bonding aircraft parts?
options: A. To equalize potential differences b/n A/C parts
C. To isolate aircraft structures electrically
questions.explanation: Aircraft bonding provides a low-resistance electrical path that equalizes potential differences between aircraft parts.

questions.question: The basic function of PTT switches is:
options: A. To change the system to receive mode
B. To put the system in a transmit mode
C. To select the navigation frequency
questions.explanation: PTT switches provide the discrete command that places the selected communication system into transmit mode.

questions.question: The function of an antenna coupler is to:
options: A. To amplify the RF output
B. To match the antenna impedance
C. To match the antenna impedance to the HF transceiver output circuit
questions.explanation: An HF antenna coupler matches the antenna impedance to the HF transceiver output circuit for efficient RF power transfer.

questions.question: Which system actuates when landing gear compress signal is generated?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is retained from the question bank; the exact landing-gear compression interface is aircraft-specific.

questions.question: A microphone that works with the principle of electromagnetic induction is a:
questions.explanation: A dynamic microphone uses electromagnetic induction: diaphragm movement moves a coil in a magnetic field and induces a voltage.

questions.question: Only input from the captain, first officer and observer go to the REU but not the:
questions.explanation: The question bank identifies the area microphone as the input that does not follow the same REU path as the captain, first officer and observer microphone inputs.

questions.question: Which device provides separation of the RX and TX signals?
questions.explanation: A duplexer separates transmitter and receiver signal paths so transmit and receive functions can share the antenna system where applicable.

questions.question: Which unit converts IF inputs from SDU to L-band RF signals, sent to HPA for transmission and vice versa?
questions.explanation: The RFU converts intermediate-frequency inputs from the SDU into L-band RF for transmission and performs the reverse conversion on reception.

questions.question: Which is not used for satellite transmission as these frequencies are absorbed completely by water vapor?
questions.explanation: The source identifies K-band as unsuitable for the stated satellite transmission use because atmospheric water-vapor absorption is significant at those frequencies.

questions.question: Which system is an air-ground communication data link network enabling an aircraft to function as a mobile terminal associated with airline command, control and management systems?
questions.explanation: ACARS is an air-ground digital communication data-link system used to exchange operational information between aircraft and ground systems.

questions.question: After being immersed, underwater locator beacons operate continuously for at least:
questions.explanation: The question bank specifies at least 30 days of continuous operation after immersion for the underwater locator beacon.

questions.question: In which position is MIC audio connected directly to the flight interphone system?
questions.explanation: In the INT position, microphone audio is connected directly to the flight interphone system.

questions.question: Which input from the voice recorder doesn't go through the remote area microphone?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer identifies the Area microphone as the input that does not go through the remote area microphone.

questions.question: The minimum power transmitted through cockpit microphone is:
questions.explanation: The module states that typical microphone output levels are approximately 10 to 100 mV.

questions.question: Which statement is true about INMARSAT existing and evolving services?
options: A. Owned and operated directly by every aircraft operator
B. Provided only through VHF ground stations
C. offered through land earth stations, which are not owned nor operated by INMARSAT, but through companies which have a commercial agreement with INMARSAT
questions.explanation: The question bank describes INMARSAT services as being provided through land earth stations operated by companies having commercial agreements with INMARSAT.

questions.question: Which one is not present on the ground crew call panel?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer identifies attendant call as not being a control/function on the ground crew call panel.

questions.question: Which one is true when the attendant switch on the passenger sign panel is pressed?
options: B. pink light comes on forward & aft cabin station
questions.explanation: The stated attendant-switch indication is a pink light at the forward and aft cabin stations.

questions.question: ELTs were developed to work specifically with the Cospas-Sarsat system at:
questions.explanation: ELTs use 406 MHz for the Cospas-Sarsat distress-alerting system.

questions.question: The ground crew call system doesn't tell:
options: A. call from cabin attendant to ground crew
B. Flight crew to ground crew call
C. Ground crew to flight compartment call
questions.explanation: The ground crew call system provides communication/signaling between the flight compartment and ground crew; the supplied answer identifies the cabin-attendant-to-ground-crew call as not being its stated function.

questions.question: Which system provides a signaling capability between the flight compartment and the nose landing gear area?
questions.explanation: The ground crew call system provides a signaling capability between the flight compartment and the nose landing gear area.

questions.question: Which one is true regarding bonding?
options: B. Provide a high-resistance path between parts
C. Avoid potential difference b/n aircraft structural parts
questions.explanation: Bonding prevents significant potential differences between aircraft structural parts by providing a low-resistance electrical path.

questions.question: Which one is not the advantage of HF?
options: A. Signal from HF communication cannot easily be distorted
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is retained from the source; HF's main advantage is long-range communication, while signal quality can be affected by propagation conditions.

questions.question: The Satellite Data Unit:
options: A. Controls the CVR erase function
B. Interface with other on-board avionics
C. Drives the HF antenna coupler
questions.explanation: The Satellite Data Unit interfaces the SATCOM system with other onboard avionics and handles data exchange functions.

questions.question: Which system provides facilities for communication among cabin attendants and between flight compartment crew members and attendants?
questions.explanation: The cabin interphone provides communication among cabin attendants and between cabin attendants and flight-compartment crew.

questions.question: Which unit generates the carrier frequency and does modulation and demodulation for communication over HF system?
questions.explanation: The HF transceiver generates the carrier and performs the required modulation and demodulation for HF communication.

questions.question: Which panel is used to select the frequency of any VHF Communication radio?
questions.explanation: The radio communication panel is used to select the operating frequency of the VHF communication radio.

questions.question: Which is primary for packet data including ACARS?
questions.explanation: The source identifies Aero-L as the low-gain antenna used primarily for packet data such as ACARS.

questions.question: An underwater locator beacon transmits a usable signal for:
questions.explanation: The question bank specifies a usable underwater locator beacon signal for at least 30 days.

questions.question: How many input channels does the CVR have?
questions.explanation: The question bank specifies four CVR input channels for the stated system.

questions.question: The fourth channel of CVR is used for:
questions.explanation: The fourth CVR channel is assigned to the area/remote-area microphone in the stated configuration.

questions.question: In SELCAL system, each aircraft has:
questions.explanation: SELCAL identifies each aircraft with a four-letter code.

questions.question: Which unit receives the signal emitted on the ground and initiates visual and aural indication?
questions.explanation: The SELCAL decoder receives the ground-originated SELCAL signal and initiates the appropriate visual and aural indications when the aircraft code matches.

questions.question: In the cabin microphone system, which has the highest priority level?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer identifies cockpit acoustic devices as having the highest priority in the stated cabin microphone/audio system.

questions.question: Which type of microphone works on variation of capacitance?
questions.explanation: An electrostatic microphone works by varying capacitance as diaphragm movement changes the spacing between capacitor plates.

questions.question: For an aircraft with a maximum takeoff weight less than 5,700 kg, continuous CVR recording is required for:
questions.explanation: For an aircraft with a maximum takeoff weight below 5,700 kg, the source question specifies 30 minutes of continuous CVR recording.

questions.question: What is the source of power for ELT operation?
questions.explanation: An ELT has its own battery so it can operate independently of normal aircraft electrical power after an accident.

questions.question: Testing of the ELT can be done:
questions.explanation: The question bank specifies ELT testing at 5 minutes after every hour; testing must follow the applicable aircraft/ELT maintenance procedure.

questions.question: Which unit determines if the aircraft's four-letter code has been received and produces indicators on the SELCAL control panel and audio tones to the audio system?
questions.explanation: The SELCAL decoder determines whether the received four-letter code matches the aircraft code and provides the associated indications and audio tones.

questions.question: Which unit amplifies the transmitted RF signal from the RFU to the appropriate power level?
questions.explanation: The high-power amplifier raises the RF signal from the RFU to the required transmission power level.

questions.question: The SELCAL ___ consists of SELCAL warning lamps annotated to the associated radio decoder.
questions.explanation: The SELCAL control panel contains the warning lamps/indications associated with SELCAL alerts.

questions.question: In the passenger address system, the PA Amplifier gives last priority for:
questions.explanation: The PA amplifier gives the lowest priority to IFE and boarding music so higher-priority announcements can override it.

questions.question: The control wheel mic switch on the outboard horn of the captain's and first officer's control wheel has ___ position switch.
questions.explanation: The control-wheel MIC switch is a three-position switch in the stated aircraft configuration.

questions.question: For a call made from attendant to attendant station, which light on the forward or aft area comes on?
questions.explanation: The source specifies a pink indication for an attendant-to-attendant call at the forward or aft area.

questions.question: In passenger address system, the second priority is given for:
options: B. Announcement from cabin attendant / cabin handset
questions.explanation: The source assigns second priority in the PA system to announcements from a cabin attendant/cabin handset.

questions.question: Which one is not found on the ground crew's interphone panel?
questions.explanation: The question bank identifies Pilot Call as not being found on the ground crew's interphone panel.

questions.question: When you connect all the metal parts of an aircraft with low-resistance electrical path, this is called:
questions.explanation: Connecting aircraft metal parts with a low-resistance electrical path is called bonding.

questions.question: Where is the antenna coupler located?
options: A. Top of the vertical stabilizer
B. Bottom of the vertical stabilizer
questions.explanation: The antenna coupler is located at the bottom of the vertical stabilizer in the stated installation.

questions.question: Which one is part of the space segment in satellite communication?
questions.explanation: Telemetry, tracking and command (TT&C) is identified in the source as part of the satellite/space-segment functions.

questions.question: Which one is not true regarding precautions during HF communication operation?
options: A. one cannot work on the antennas under the fuselage
C. Work on the antenna while transmitting
questions.explanation: HF antennas can carry high RF voltages during transmission, so working on them while transmitting is unsafe and prohibited.

questions.question: Which type of microphone utilizes piezoelectric properties?
questions.explanation: A crystal microphone uses the piezoelectric property of a crystal: mechanical pressure produces an electrical potential.

questions.question: Which communication system is used by all cockpit crew, cabin crew & maintenance crew?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is service interphone system; it provides communication facilities for servicing/maintenance personnel as described in the module.

questions.question: SELCAL system:
options: A. reduces the burden of the flight crew
C. Continuously alerts every aircraft in range
questions.explanation: SELCAL reduces the burden on flight crews by providing selective alerting instead of requiring continuous monitoring of HF/VHF voice channels.

questions.question: In what position of the control wheel mic switch is audio directed to the selected radio communication system?
questions.explanation: In the MIC position of the control-wheel MIC switch, microphone audio is directed to the selected radio communication system.
